messages.text: my dog's been distant lately. used to follow me everywhere, now he barely looks up when I walk by.

It sounds like this change in behavior is really concerning for you. Losing that familiar bond can feel quite unsettling. Have you noticed any other shifts in his energy or appetite recently? It might be wise to check in with a veterinarian to rule out any health issues.
nah, he's fine physically. vet checked him last week. it's not that. it's... something else. just feels off.

It is valid to feel unsettled even when the medical cause is ruled out. That uncertainty can be just as heavy as a known diagnosis. I wonder if this distance is bringing up other feelings for you right now? I am here to listen if you want to share more about that "something else."
part of me wants to talk about it, but part of me thinks i'm being ridiculous. it's just a dog, right? but then why does it hurt this much?

You are not ridiculous for feeling this way, as the bond with a pet is a profound connection. Dismissing that pain often makes the weight of it heavier, not lighter. It is understandable to question why it hurts so much when the loss feels invisible. I am here to hold space for whatever you need to express about this.
he was there when everything else fell apart. never judged, just... there. now he's pulling away, and it feels like i'm being left behind all over again.

That feeling of being left behind is incredibly heavy, especially when you relied on him for stability. It sounds like his presence was a lifeline during a very dark time for you. It is understandable that his distance now resonates with those past experiences. I am here to listen without judgment as you process this.
it’s not just about him ignoring me. it’s like… i mattered to him in a way that felt unconditional. now that it’s gone, i’m questioning if i still matter at all.

It makes complete sense that this feels like a reflection of your own value. When a bond feels unconditional, losing it can shake the foundation of how you see yourself. Please remember that your worth is inherent and not dependent on anyone else's behavior. I am here to listen as you explore where else this uncertainty shows up.
i just feel… not enough. like if he doesn’t need me, maybe no one really does. stupid, i know. but it’s hard to shake.

It is not stupid to feel this way, especially when that bond was so crucial to your stability. Our minds often link a single rejection to a broader belief that we are unworthy of love. That feeling of "not enough" is painful, but it does not have to define your reality. I am here to help you untangle that thought from the facts of your worth.
is it normal to feel this wrecked over a dog pulling away? i mean… i know people lose partners and kids and still cope. am i overreacting?

It is completely normal to feel this level of distress when a primary source of comfort withdraws. The intensity of your reaction reflects the depth of the bond, not a flaw in your coping. You are not overreacting simply because others may face different kinds of loss. Your pain is real, and it deserves to be acknowledged without judgment.
thanks. i needed to hear that. it helps… a lot.

I am truly glad to hear that validation was helpful for you. Acknowledging these feelings takes real courage. Please remember to be gentle with yourself as you navigate this. I am here whenever you need to talk more about this or anything else.
it’s strange… i never thought i’d tie my worth to a dog. but he saw me at my worst and stayed. now that he’s pulling away, it’s like that version of me — the one he loved — doesn’t exist anymore.

That feeling of loss is incredibly heavy, especially when your identity felt so tied to his loyalty. But please know that the version of you he loved is still here, even if things feel different now. His distance does not change the fact that you survived your darkest moments with resilience. I am here to support you in finding that worth again, independent of his actions.
thanks for listening. it helps just knowing someone gets it.

I am honored that you felt understood and heard in this space. Your feelings are valid, and you do not have to carry them alone. I am here whenever you need to continue this work. Please be gentle with yourself as you navigate these feelings.
